text: dsh-skill-scope 是面向 DSH Web 的 Skill 与 MCP 管理插件。它在侧栏提供全局面板，并在输入区提供工作区入口；服务端按全局和项目策略调整 Agent 可调用的能力。用户可搜索、筛选和启停 Skill、MCP，并让工作区逐项覆盖全局默认值。修改在 Agent 创建或能力清单变化时应用，保存后也会尝试更新当前会话。适合希望按项目控制 Agent 能力的用户。安装后不需额外 API 密钥，策略保存在本机。

dsh-skill-scope manages Skill and MCP visibility in DSH Web. Its global panel and workspace controls let users search, toggle, and override capabilities per project. Policies apply when agents are created or inventories change. Settings stay local; no extra API key is needed.

How can I hide selected skills from the model while keeping them installed?

dsh-skill-scope 的功能「全局能力面板」：在 DSH 侧栏打开全局 Skill 与 MCP 清单。用户可搜索、筛选并切换项目默认可用状态，也可控制是否显示官方 Skill。
dsh-skill-scope 的功能「工作区覆盖」：在空白会话的输入区入口打开项目弹层，逐项启用或关闭 Skill 和 MCP。未单独设置的项目项跟随全局状态，修改保存在工作区策略中。
dsh-skill-scope 的功能「Agent 能力收窄」：创建 Agent 时读取全局和当前工作区策略，并将被关闭的 Skill 与 MCP 工具从该 Agent 的可调用集合中收窄；清单变化时重新应用策略。
dsh-skill-scope 的功能「策略 API 与保存反馈」：面板通过四条 POST 路由读取或保存全局、工作区策略；工作区请求携带会话 ID，保存后会尝试将新策略应用到当前会话。

section: 安装

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · 它解决什么问题：你在 DSH 里装得越多，Agent 每一轮要读的清单就越长。

- 用户级 Skill 目录里堆了 **N+ Skill**，其中能帮到当前这个任务的只有几个。
- 每个 MCP server 都会把它的**全部工具**塞进模型的工具表，哪怕这一轮一个都用不上。
- 写代码的工程和写文章的工作区，需要的 Skill 和 MCP **根本不是同一套**。
- 你想「这个项目就用这几个能力」，但官方没有给任何开关——Skill 装上就是全局可见。

后果不是"不好看"，而是实打实的成本：

| 代价 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| **烧 Token** | Skill 目录与 MCP 工具表每一轮都要重新进上下文，装的越多，每一轮固定开销越大 |
| **注意力被稀释** | 候选太多，模型更容易选错工具、漏掉真正相关的那个 |
| **上下文不干净** | 无关能力混进提示词，结果更难预测，调试更难 |
| **工程之间互相污染** | A 项目的专用能力，在 B 项目里也一直占着位置 |
section: 它解决什么问题

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · 1. 全局面板——一次收掉所有工程都不需要的能力：点左侧栏的「**全局 Skills**」，打开一个原生主界面页面，列出**全局层**的全部 Skill 与 MCP server。
在这里关掉的名字**默认对所有工作区生效**；某个工程确实需要时，可以在本工程里单独把它打开（见下文第 3 条）。

上图红圈标出两个入口：左侧栏的 **Global Skills**，和输入框右下角的 **Workspace Skills**。

- 顶部一排是**视图切换**（全部 / 已启用 / 已禁用）——它只筛列表，不改任何开关。
- 搜索框**同时筛 Skill 与 MCP 两段**，输入即过滤。
- 列表按来源分组折叠，长清单也能快速定位。
section: 1. 全局面板——一次收掉所有工程都不需要的能力

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · 1. 全局面板——一次收掉所有工程都不需要的能力：**官方 Skill 默认不列**：`@deepseek-ai` 官方包自带的 Skill（`cordis-*` 预设、`office-*` 等）
默认不出现在面板上，模型仍可自动调用它们。想看见、想关掉它们时，打开视图条右端的
「**显示官方 Skill**」开关：这些行会回到清单，与普通行一样可以逐项关闭。
这个开关是**单机级**的（存在 `$DSH_HOME/skill-scope/global.json`），全局与本工程两个面板
都展示它、值永远一致；在工作区面板里打开它，效果同样对所有工程生效。

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · 2. 本工程面板——只给这一个项目留要用的能力：在**新会话**的输入框右下角点「**工作区 Skills**」，打开本工程弹层（浮动在当前界面之上）：

图中列表标题写明「只影响 default-workspace」，下半部分按来源分组：本例里 `.agents` 目录贡献 35 项。

- 列表与全局面板**同一份清单**：全局关掉的项也在里面（开关是关的），你可以直接在这里把它打开。
- 与全局设置不同的行带一个红色标记「**与全局不同**」，一眼看出这个工程动过什么。
- 视图条除「全部 / 已启用 / 已禁用」外多一个「**与全局不同**」：点它只剩本工程改过的项（清单长时好用）。
- 改动**只对本工程的新会话生效**，不影响别的项目。
section: 2. 本工程面板——只给这一个项目留要用的能力

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · 3. 关键规则：全局给默认值，工程可以逐项改：```text
      磁盘上的全部 Skill 与 MCP
                │
                ▼
      ┌─────────────────────┐

每一项在本工程里有三种状态。界面上只有开关一种动作，因为「跟随全局」用**不记这条**来表达：

| 状态 | 含义 | 界面上怎么看出来 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 跟随全局 | 本工程对这项没有主张 | 开关位置与全局一致，没有红标 |
| 本工程打开 | 全局关着，这个工程要用 | 开关是开的 + 红标「与全局不同」 |
| 本工程关闭 | 全局开着，这个工程不要 | 开关是关的 + 红标「与全局不同」 |

想改回「跟随全局」：把开关拨回全局的样子即可，红标消失，这条决定也随之删除。
section: 3. 关键规则：全局给默认值，工程可以逐项改

section: Installation

text: @dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · The problem it solves：The more you install in DSH, the longer the list your agent has to read every turn.
section: The problem it solves

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · The problem it solves：- Your user-level skill directory accumulates **N+ skills**, of which only a few help the task at hand.
- Every MCP server pushes **all of its tools** into the model's tool table, even when none are used this turn.
- A coding project and a writing workspace need **entirely different** skills and MCP servers.
- You want "this project uses only these capabilities", but there is no switch for that — an installed skill is globally visible.

The cost is not cosmetic. It is real:
section: The problem it solves

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · The problem it solves：| Cost | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **Burned tokens** | The skill list and the MCP tool table re-enter context every turn; the more you install, the higher the fixed per-turn overhead |
| **Diluted attention** | Too many candidates make the model likelier to pick the wrong tool or miss the relevant one |
| **An unclean context** | Unrelated capabilities mixed into the prompt make results harder to predict and harder to debug |
| **Cross-project contamination** | A capability only project A needs keeps occupying space in project B |
section: The problem it solves

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · 1. The global panel — switch off everything no project needs：**Official skills are hidden by default**: the skills shipped by `@deepseek-ai` packages
(`cordis-*` presets, `office-*` and so on) do not appear in the panel, and the model can still
call them. To see them — or to switch them off — turn on **Show official skills** at the right end
of the view bar: those rows come back into the list and can be switched off one by one like any
other row. The switch is per machine (stored in `$DSH_HOME/skill-scope/global.json`); both the
global panel and the project panel show it, they always read the same value, and turning it on
from either panel affects every workspace.
section: 1. The global panel — switch off everything no project needs

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · 2. The project panel — keep only what this one project needs：In a **new session**, click **Workspace Skills** at the bottom right of the input box to open the project-scoped overlay (it floats above the current view):

The panel title states that it affects `default-workspace` only, and the lower part groups items by source: in this example the `.agents` directory contributes 35 of them.
section: 2. The project panel — keep only what this one project needs

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · 2. The project panel — keep only what this one project needs：- This list holds **the same inventory as the global panel**: items switched off globally are here too (with the switch off), and you can switch them on right here.
- A row that differs from the global setting carries a red **"Differs from global"** tag, so you can see at a glance what this project has changed.
- Besides **All / Enabled / Disabled**, the view bar has a fourth button, **Differs from global**: it narrows the list to what this project changed, which helps once the inventory gets long.
- Changes **apply only to new sessions in this project** and affect no other project.
section: 2. The project panel — keep only what this one project needs

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · 3. The key rule: global supplies defaults, a project overrides item by item：```text
      Every skill and MCP server on disk
                │
                ▼
      ┌─────────────────────┐

Each item has one of three states in a project. The panel exposes a single control, because
"follow global" is expressed by **not recording that item**:
section: 3. The key rule: global supplies defaults, a project overrides item by item

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · 3. The key rule: global supplies defaults, a project overrides item by item：| State | Meaning | How the panel shows it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Follow global | This project has no opinion on the item | Switch sits at the global position, no red tag |
| Switched on here | Off globally, but this project needs it | Switch is on + red tag "Differs from global" |
| Switched off here | On globally, but this project does not want it | Switch is off + red tag "Differs from global" |
section: 3. The key rule: global supplies defaults, a project overrides item by item

text:
@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · 3. The key rule: global supplies defaults, a project overrides item by item：To go back to "follow global", move the switch to the global position: the red tag disappears and the
record is dropped.
section: 3. The key rule: global supplies defaults, a project overrides item by item

@dotdance/dsh-skill-scope README · Off is not deleted: manual invocation always remains：Switching a skill off only disables its **automatic invocation by the model**. You can still call it by typing `/name` in a session.
